title: malus × brevipes
intro: Malus × brevipes, commonly known as the Brie apple, is a hybrid plant species within the Malus genus, derived from the cross between Malus baccata and Malus communis. The Brie apple is valued for its potential health benefits, including antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, which may contribute to the prevention of chronic diseases such as heart disease and certain types of cancer. The plant's therapeutic actions are attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which have been shown to exhibit antimicrobial, antiviral, and antiseptic properties. Furthermore, the Brie apple's bioactive constituents may also contribute to its potential use in traditional medicine for treating various ailments, including digestive issues and skin conditions.
